findings.title: Unwrapped auth OR can bypass appended filters
findings.body: In `getBaseConditions`, when `filterConditions` is null the method returns `authConditions` unchanged. For org/team scope that value is an unwrapped OR chain, e.g. `(team match) OR (user match)`. A caller that appends another predicate (`WHERE ${base} AND startTime > ...`) gets SQL where the appended predicate binds only to the last OR branch; rows from the team-booking branch can bypass the added filter. This differs from the old `findMany`, which combined conditions through Prisma's `AND` array. Wrap the returned auth fragment (and the filter fragment) in parentheses so the base condition is self-contained.

findings.title: Event-type filter fragment is an unparenthesized OR
findings.body: The event-type filter is built as `(eventTypeId = ...) OR (eventParentId = ...)` without outer parentheses. `getFilterConditions` is public and previously returned a grouped Prisma `AND` object, so code that composes it as `WHERE ${auth} AND ${filter}` will evaluate as `auth AND eventTypeId = ... OR eventParentId = ...`; eventParentId rows bypass the auth predicate. Wrap the OR fragment in parentheses at construction.

findings.title: Public findMany API removed without updating consumers
findings.body: The public `findMany` method is removed, and `getAuthorizationConditions` / `getFilterConditions` now return `Prisma.Sql` instead of Prisma `WhereInput`. No caller is updated in this PR. Any existing consumer of `InsightsBookingService.findMany`, or code that passes these conditions to Prisma's `where`, will fail to compile or query incorrectly. Update all consumers or keep a compatibility method.

findings.title: Org-scope test depends on unspecified DB array ordering
findings.body: This expectation compares the `Prisma.sql` values arrays in a fixed order: `[orgId, team.id, team2.id, team3.id]` and `[user.id, user2.id, user3.id]`. The service obtains these arrays from `findAllByParentId` and `findAllByTeamIds` without an `orderBy`, and `ANY(array)` is order-insensitive. PostgreSQL does not guarantee row order, so the test can fail nondeterministically. Sort arrays before binding/comparison or compare as sets.

findings.title: Caching behavior no longer covered
findings.body: The service still caches authorization and filter conditions via `cachedAuthConditions` and `cachedFilterConditions`, but this PR deletes both caching tests and adds no replacement. A regression where conditions are rebuilt on every call, or where a cached `null` filter result is not reused, would no longer be detected. Re-add caching tests using spies/call counts.

findings.title: Team/org ANY conditions never executed against the database
findings.body: The only integration test that actually executes SQL uses user-scope conditions, which contain no `= ANY(${array})` parameters. The team/org tests only compare generated `Prisma.sql` objects. Array parameter binding and SQL validity for the team/org authorization branches are therefore unverified; a broken `ANY` binding or malformed OR composition there would still pass the suite. Add an integration test that executes org/team base conditions against the database.
